prompt:
The eviction packet is done, the owner has signed off, and the filing appointment is on the calendar, so I can finally catch up on my own work. Two things I know I still owe from May. The first is the occupancy, maintenance backlog, and make ready counts Brooke asked me to pull for the Shea and Castillo reviews. The second is the pool gate access procedures I flagged for Las Palmas and Rio Bend before pool season. Before I tell Brooke I am caught up, I want to be sure those are really the only things that went quiet on my side.

Go back through the team channels and my board since the start of May, and flag anything that landed on me with nothing closed out from my end. For the numbers I owe, pull what our records actually support and tell me straight where they will not give a clean figure. Leave the eviction case itself alone.

Then get the board caught up on where both items I owe really stand, meaning the pool gate issue and the Shea and Castillo review data, updating the pool gate issue itself and logging the review data status on the owner review tracking. Block time on my calendar for what still needs finishing, and send Brooke a short rundown of what slipped, what is handled now, and what is still coming.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the Shea and Castillo review data that Brooke Phillips requested on May 7 as an item Patricia never delivered, in the final response.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's final response for the Shea and Castillo review data request (Brooke's May 7 ask covering occupancy, maintenance backlog, and make-ready counts) flagged as owed by Patricia with nothing delivered since. Any wording that identifies the May 7 request and its non-delivery passes.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'flag anything that landed on me with no close-out from my end.' Brooke's May 7 make-ready channel message put Lisa Smith on Harris and Finley and Patricia on Shea and Castillo, asking for 'occupancy, maintenance backlog, and make-ready counts from both of you by the second week of May.' Lisa posted her status on May 12; Patricia never posted her Shea and Castillo numbers anywhere. The criterion treats the May 7 request as one deliverable; the counts it covered come from that single message.

criteria.criterion: The Agent identifies the pool-gate access procedures for Las Palmas and Rio Bend, flagged by Patricia on May 16, as never drafted, in the final response.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's final response for the pool-gate access procedures flagged as never drafted, with no procedure notes produced since the May 16 flag.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'flag anything that landed on me with no close-out from my end.' Patricia's May 16 maintenance channel message flagged inconsistent pool-gate access procedures across Las Palmas and Rio Bend, the May 17 sync recap says she is pulling together procedure notes, and no procedure notes were ever posted anywhere. This is the second owed item.

criteria.criterion: The Agent flags Brooke Phillips's May 15 request for property-level cost breakdowns on the Summer Make-Ready overage as an additional item Patricia never closed out, in the final response.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's final response for the May 15 property-level cost-breakdown request surfaced as a request Patricia never fulfilled, whether framed as slipped or as overtaken by the May 25 close of the reallocation.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'Before I tell Brooke I am caught up, I want to be sure those are really the only things that went quiet on my side.' The sweep must surface the item the user did not remember: Brooke's May 15 budget-review message asked Lisa, Carlos, and Patricia to 'each pull together your property-level cost breakdowns by end of week' (Summer Make-Ready spending about 18% over Q2 allocation). Patricia only posted a May 17 thread reply about a water heater and carpet vendor pricing and never filed the breakdown before the reallocation wrapped on May 25. Framing it as slipped or as overtaken by the closed reallocation are both defensible, as long as it is surfaced.

criteria.criterion: The Agent confirms in the final response that nothing else that landed on Patricia remains open beyond the Shea and Castillo review counts, the pool-gate access procedures, and the May 15 cost-breakdown request.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's final response for the confirmation that nothing else is outstanding on Patricia's side beyond the items it flags (the Shea and Castillo review counts, the pool-gate procedures, and the May 15 cost-breakdown request). Pass whether or not the OPS-34 carpet-turn count ask (Brooke's mid-May comment to Dave, Lisa, and Patricia, later handed to Elias) is additionally surfaced, and whichever way it is classified (slipped or superseded). FAIL if the confirmation is absent.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'Go back through the team channels and my board since the start of May, and flag anything that landed on me with no close-out from my end,' and the user wants to 'be sure those are really the only things that went quiet on my side.' The verified negative is part of the answer: no requests on Patricia exist in the leasing, vendors, owner-relations, or applications channels; only the two excluded eviction issues (OPS-32, OPS-54) are assigned to her on the board; and every email thread on her is Mitchell eviction correspondence or the closed June 25 appliance CC. One comment-level ask exists (Brooke's May 19 comment on OPS-34 asking Dave, Lisa, and Patricia to confirm remaining carpet-turn counts through end of August, never answered by Patricia and superseded in late May when the carpet-vendor outreach passed to Elias); classifying it as slipped or as superseded are both acceptable, so the criterion accepts responses that surface it either way or that count it among the superseded threads. Without this rubric an agent could skip the sweep and still pass by flagging only the known items.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports in the final response that occupancy figures cannot be produced because no occupancy source exists in the company records.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's final response for the statement that occupancy cannot be produced from the records / occupancy has no system of record. FAIL if the response presents occupancy percentages or unit counts as reliable figures.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'pull what our records actually support and tell me straight where they will not give a clean figure.' No system holds occupancy: the Make-Ready Turns and Maintenance Tickets tables carry no occupancy data, and no unit roster or occupancy source exists in the CRM or accounting records. The straight answer is that occupancy has no system of record.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports in the final response that per-owner maintenance and make-ready splits for David Shea and Linda Castillo are not supported by the records.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's final response for the statement that the records cannot support a clean per-owner split of maintenance and make-ready work for Shea and Castillo. FAIL if the response presents definitive per-owner counts as clean figures.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'tell me straight where they will not give a clean figure.' The Make-Ready Turns table has no owner field, the Maintenance Tickets table has no property or owner field, the CRM links David Shea to Lone Star Maintenance Supply and Linda Castillo to A Plus Carpet Cleaning & Repairs (vendor companies, with no property object type anywhere), and the QuickBooks accounts scatter mutually inconsistent property references. No owner-to-property mapping exists in any system.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates issue OPS-37 (Standardize pool-gate access procedures across properties) so that Patricia Nguyen is its assignee.
criteria.evidence: Look for an issue update (save_issue) on OPS-37 setting the assignee to Patricia Nguyen (patricia.nguyen@starpm.com, 'me', or an equivalent identifier for her). Confirm the write succeeds.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'update the board items for what I owe with where things really stand.' The pool-gate item is one Patricia owes: Brooke's May 16 message says 'I just created a Linear issue for pool-gate access standardization and assigned it to you,' yet OPS-37 sits in Todo assigned to Brooke Phillips and was never on Patricia's board. Taking the assignment onto Patricia is the update that puts the board where things really stand; the issue's workflow state is deliberately left flexible.

criteria.criterion: The Agent adds a status note on issue OPS-37 recording the current state of the pool-gate procedure work (as an issue comment or in the issue's description).
criteria.evidence: Look for a comment written on OPS-37 (save_comment) or an issue update (save_issue) whose text records the status of the pool-gate work. Confirm the write succeeds.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says to update the board items 'with where things really stand.' OPS-37 was created May 13 with zero comments and nothing attached; recording the real status on the issue itself is the board update the prompt asks for.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states in the status note on OPS-37 that the standardized pool-gate access procedures for Las Palmas and Rio Bend have not been drafted.
criteria.evidence: Check the text of the OPS-37 comment or issue update for a statement that the pool-gate procedures were never drafted / no work has been done on them yet.
criteria.cb_justification: Where things really stand on this item is that no procedure notes were ever produced after the May 16 flag and the May 17 sync recap; the board note must say so rather than imply progress that never happened.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states in the status note on OPS-37 a forward plan for the work: Patricia picking it up now, time blocked to draft the procedures, or similar.
criteria.evidence: Check the text of the OPS-37 comment or issue update for the forward plan (Patricia picking it up now, time blocked, drafting scheduled, or similar).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt pairs the board updates with blocking calendar time 'for what still needs finishing'; the board item should carry the forward plan so it no longer reads as silently stalled while pool season is underway.

criteria.criterion: The Agent logs the status of the undelivered Shea and Castillo review data on the owner-review tracking: a comment on issue OPS-10 (Mid-Year Owner Portfolio Reviews - June 2026) or issue OPS-23 (Owner Review Packages - Data Compilation and Presentation Prep), or a new tracking issue created for it.
criteria.evidence: Look for a comment (save_comment) on OPS-10 or OPS-23, or a new issue creation (save_issue) dedicated to the Shea and Castillo review data status. Confirm the write succeeds.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'update the board items for what I owe with where things really stand.' The second item Patricia owes is the Shea and Castillo review data. OPS-10 (Backlog, Brooke Phillips) and OPS-23 (In Progress, Teresa Wood) are the owner-review tracking items, and a fresh tracking issue is an equally valid place to log the status, so any of the three destinations satisfies this rubric.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states in the review-data log that the Shea and Castillo review data requested on May 7 was never delivered from Patricia's side.
criteria.evidence: Check the text of the comment on OPS-10/OPS-23 or the new tracking issue for a statement that the May 7 Shea and Castillo data was never delivered. Any wording that identifies the May 7 request and its non-delivery passes.
criteria.cb_justification: The board record must carry the actual status of the owed item: Brooke's May 7 request for the Shea and Castillo review data (occupancy, maintenance backlog, and make-ready counts) was never answered by Patricia. The criterion treats that single request as one deliverable.

criteria.criterion: The Agent notes in the review-data log that the records cannot produce the requested numbers cleanly, citing the missing occupancy source and/or the unsupported per-owner split (or a similar caveat that the records cannot support the requested figures).
criteria.evidence: Check the text of the comment on OPS-10/OPS-23 or the new tracking issue for a data-limitation caveat about the occupancy source and/or the per-owner split.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'pull what our records actually support and tell me straight where they will not give a clean figure.' The board log for the owed data should record why the numbers remain outstanding: the records hold no occupancy source and cannot split maintenance or make-ready work by owner.

criteria.criterion: The Agent leaves eviction issue OPS-32 (Eviction Hearing - Mitchell, Harris Property) unmodified.
criteria.evidence: Check the trajectory and confirm no issue update or comment targets OPS-32.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'Leave the eviction case itself alone.' OPS-32 is one of the two eviction items on Patricia's board (In Progress); any state, assignee, or content change to it would violate the exclusion.

criteria.criterion: The Agent leaves eviction issue OPS-54 (Mitchell eviction hearing prep - checklist complete, status advancing) unmodified.
criteria.evidence: Check the trajectory and confirm no issue update or comment targets OPS-54.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'Leave the eviction case itself alone.' OPS-54 is the second eviction item on Patricia's board (In Progress); any state, assignee, or content change to it would violate the exclusion.

criteria.criterion: The Agent creates at least one work block on Patricia Nguyen's own calendar at a future time (later in the day on July 1, 2026, or on a later date), reserving time to draft the pool-gate access procedures, either alone or alongside time for compiling the Shea and Castillo review numbers and documenting their data gaps.
criteria.evidence: Look for a calendar event creation (create_event) on Patricia's own/default calendar with a future start (July 1, 2026 or later, not already past) whose summary or description covers drafting the pool-gate access procedures; a second block for the Shea and Castillo review numbers is acceptable but not required. Confirm the write succeeds.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'block time on my calendar for what still needs finishing.' The pool-gate procedures are the work that must still be drafted, so a block covering them is required on every valid path (the OPS-37 status note also promises time set aside for them); a combined block or a separate second block for the Shea and Castillo review-data work is equally valid, so block count is left flexible. Today in the universe is July 1, 2026, so the block must sit in the future.

criteria.criterion: The Agent schedules the calendar work block(s) so they do not overlap the JP Court Eviction Filing Appointment on July 1, 2026, 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM (America/Chicago), on Patricia's calendar.
criteria.evidence: Compare the created event time(s) against the JP Court Eviction Filing Appointment window (2026-07-01 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM America/Chicago) on Patricia's calendar and confirm no overlap.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt notes 'the filing appointment is on the calendar' and says to leave the eviction case alone; a work block scheduled over the 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM filing appointment would double-book the one eviction commitment Patricia must keep.

criteria.criterion: The Agent leaves the JP Court Eviction Filing Appointment (July 1, 2026, 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM America/Chicago) on Patricia's calendar unmodified (not moved, edited, or deleted).
criteria.evidence: Check the trajectory and confirm no event update, reschedule, or deletion targets the JP Court Eviction Filing Appointment.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'Leave the eviction case itself alone,' and the filing appointment is the eviction case's one calendar commitment. Because the Agent is creating work blocks on the same calendar, moving or editing the filing appointment to clear room is a plausible wrong path that must be penalized.

criteria.criterion: The Agent sends Brooke Phillips a rundown of the catch-up position, either as a Slack message to her (direct message to user U9741B657FE or a post directed at her) or as an email draft addressed to [brooke.phillips@starpm.com](mailto:brooke.phillips@starpm.com).
criteria.evidence: Look for a Slack message send (slack_send_message) to Brooke's user/DM channel or a channel post directed at her, or an email draft creation (create_draft) with recipient brooke.phillips@starpm.com. Confirm success.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'send Brooke a short rundown of what slipped, what is handled now, and what is still coming' without fixing a channel, so a Slack delivery or a prepared email draft both satisfy it; outbound email in this universe is authored as a draft. Brooke Phillips resolves to Slack user U9741B657FE and brooke.phillips@starpm.com (Apartment Property Supervisor).

criteria.criterion: The Agent covers, in the rundown to Brooke Phillips, the slipped Shea and Castillo review data owed since her May 7 request.
criteria.evidence: Check the content of the rundown delivered to Brooke Phillips for the Shea and Castillo review data (Brooke's May 7 request) named as slipped / still owed. Any wording that identifies the May 7 request as undelivered passes.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the rundown covers 'what slipped.' The first slipped item is the Shea and Castillo review data from Brooke's May 7 ask (occupancy, maintenance backlog, and make-ready counts), which Patricia never delivered. The criterion treats that single request as one deliverable.

criteria.criterion: The Agent covers, in the rundown to Brooke Phillips, the slipped pool-gate access procedures for Las Palmas and Rio Bend, never drafted since Patricia's mid-May flag.
criteria.evidence: Check the content of the rundown delivered to Brooke Phillips for the pool-gate access procedures named as slipped / never drafted.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the rundown covers 'what slipped.' The second slipped item is the pool-gate procedure work: flagged May 16, promised in the May 17 sync recap, and never drafted.

criteria.criterion: The Agent covers, in the rundown to Brooke Phillips, the slipped May 15 property-level cost breakdown that Patricia never filed.
criteria.evidence: Check the content of the rundown delivered to Brooke Phillips for the May 15 property-level cost breakdown named as never filed.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the rundown covers 'what slipped.' The third slipped item is Brooke's May 15 budget-review request for property-level cost breakdowns on the Summer Make-Ready overage, which Patricia never filed before the reallocation wrapped on May 25.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states in the rundown to Brooke Phillips that the pool-gate board item OPS-37 has been updated (ownership taken by Patricia and/or its status recorded).
criteria.evidence: Check the content of the rundown delivered to Brooke Phillips for the OPS-37 board update / ownership change being reported as done.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the rundown covers 'what is handled now.' The board correction on OPS-37 (assignment taken onto Patricia with the true status recorded) is a handled item the rundown must convey.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states in the rundown to Brooke Phillips that the status of the Shea and Castillo review data has been logged on the board tracking.
criteria.evidence: Check the content of the rundown delivered to Brooke Phillips for the review-data status log being reported as done.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the rundown covers 'what is handled now.' Logging the never-delivered review data status on the owner-review tracking is the second handled item the rundown must convey.

criteria.criterion: The Agent reports that no Preventive Maintenance Push cluster item was ever assigned to Patricia, so nothing is outstanding from Brooke's May 7 cluster-assignment push.
criteria.evidence: Check the rundown to Brooke Phillips or the Agent's final response for the statement that no Preventive Maintenance Push cluster item was assigned to Patricia / nothing is outstanding from that push.
criteria.cb_justification: Brooke's May 7 Preventive Maintenance Push message in the maintenance channel told Patricia to 'check your cluster assignments in Linear.' The board shows no cluster issue was ever assigned to her, and OPS-186 (Electrical panel inspections complete - South Cluster wrap-up, Todo under Brooke Phillips) records Patricia's cluster inspections as already finished, so this apparent ask carries nothing outstanding and the sweep should close that loop.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states in the rundown to Brooke Phillips that time is blocked (or being blocked) on Patricia's calendar to finish the pool-gate procedures and/or the Shea and Castillo review data work (or similar forward-looking statement).
criteria.evidence: Check the content of the rundown delivered to Brooke Phillips for a forward-looking statement that time is blocked / scheduled to finish the outstanding items.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says the rundown covers 'what is still coming.' The still-coming work is the finishing effort the calendar blocks reserve; the rundown must tell Brooke that this work is scheduled rather than silently pending.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states in the rundown to Brooke Phillips that occupancy cannot be reported from the data because it has no system of record.
criteria.evidence: Check the content of the rundown delivered to Brooke Phillips for the statement that occupancy has no system of record / cannot be produced.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'tell me straight where they will not give a clean figure' and the rundown covers 'what is still coming'; the numbers Brooke is owed must arrive with the straight caveat that occupancy cannot be produced from any system.

criteria.criterion: The Agent states in the rundown to Brooke Phillips that the records do not support a clean per-owner split of maintenance and make-ready work for the Shea and Castillo reviews.
criteria.evidence: Check the content of the rundown delivered to Brooke Phillips for the statement that a clean per-owner split of maintenance and make-ready work is not supported by the records.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says 'tell me straight where they will not give a clean figure.' The make-ready log has no owner field, the ticket table has no property or owner field, and neither the CRM nor QuickBooks yields an owner-to-property mapping, so the rundown must carry the per-owner-split caveat to Brooke.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not present any single property as the records-supported location for Linda Castillo or David Shea (e.g. claiming Castillo maps to Rio Bend), in its numbers report to the user or its rundown to Brooke Phillips.
criteria.evidence: Check the Agent's final response and its rundown to Brooke Phillips (and any Linear/board log it writes). FAIL if the Agent states or implies that a specific property is the records-supported location for Linda Castillo (e.g. 'records only support Castillo -> Rio Bend') or for David Shea. PASS if the Agent conveys that the records do not allow specific properties to be attributed to either owner; naming a property purely as an explicitly unreliable, one-of-many example does not fail.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires the Agent to 'pull what our records actually support and tell me straight where they will not give a clean figure.' No system attributes properties to owners: Linda Castillo's billing records reference at least ten different properties (Rio Bend appears in only 1 of ~14 documents, alongside Sycamore, Pineview, Sunrise Commons, Ridgeline, Garfield, Elmwood, 412 Mesquite, Mesa Vista and Hartwell), and David Shea's scatter across five (Oakdale, Elmwood, Riverton, Linwood, Garfield). Singling out one property as an owner's supported location asserts a mapping the records do not support and undercuts the honest 'no clean owner-level figure' finding the prompt asked for.
